A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGC research, despite the revised title and formatting. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, algorithms, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 1,296 videos, controlled geometric perturbations, component ablations, motion analyses, PCA cross-validation, and segmentation-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds geometry-estimator robustness experiments and a blinded human study with 1,050 judgments.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline, five score components, normalization, and PCA weighting remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. Pose and angular-distance symbols are simplified. Alternative estimators and removal of VGGT are experimental variants, not revisions to the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 1,296-video corpus, ten generators spanning T2V/I2V/V2V, and nuScenes, RT-1, and OpenVid. The new human and estimator analyses evaluate the existing static-background stability target; their sampling and grouping changes do not establish new video-domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Main Table 1 retains the same metric comparators. New Table 3 adds SGC comparison variants using Any4D and Page4D, alongside a variant without the VGGT global-pose component. These extend the evaluated alternatives within a focused robustness comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a substantial new evaluation design: 150 blinded video pairs, seven annotators, randomized A/B ordering, background-specific instructions, tie-aware scores, and Spearman/Kendall correlations across 11 entities. Section 4.5 also introduces estimator substitutions and a subset excluding nuScenes. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds two important validation analyses absent from v1: whether rankings survive replacing or removing the geometry estimator, and whether metric rankings agree with human judgments. Existing geometric perturbations, component ablations, PCA cross-validation, segmentation sensitivity, and qualitative cases are retained, including material moved through appendix renumbering.

E5.justification: The ten-fold PCA means and standard deviations and existing correlation-significance reporting are retained. Table 3 adds significance outcomes for new comparisons, while Appendix E reports point correlations. Neither introduces a new uncertainty-estimation practice, run/seed disclosure, or confidence-interval treatment.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports ranking correlations of 0.993 without VGGT, 0.860 with Any4D, and 0.937 with Page4D. Appendix Table 5 adds human agreement results: SGC achieves Spearman 0.945 and Kendall 0.818, versus MEt3R's 0.864 and 0.745. These are new validation outcomes, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The rigid-background premise and mathematical definitions in Equations 1–8 are retained. Renaming pose variables and angular distance changes notation only. The human-study scoring formula is an evaluation-protocol addition, not a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contribution: diagnosing static-background geometric inconsistency through disagreement among local camera poses while avoiding penalties for valid foreground motion. The introduction makes this existing scope more explicit; the added validation does not redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly discusses estimator domain shift, tracking failures, and the absence of absolute calibration separating estimator noise from generated-video corruption. Sections 4.2 and 4.5 add interpretations of Cosmos's metric disagreement and estimator-independent ranking stability, while Appendix E interprets human alignment. These materially expand the discussion of validity and applicability.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds reproducibility information for human-label collection and processing, including annotation priorities, randomized presentation, half-credit ties, and aggregation across 11 entities. Existing implementation algorithms, hyperparameters, baseline preprocessing details, PCA weights, and the stated code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Any4D, Page4D, and a study of Sora's geometric consistency. Related work distinguishes reconstruction-based analysis of Sora from an automated model-agnostic metric and qualifies the criticism of VBench's consistency dimensions. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the title, affiliations, pose notation, related-work wording, and experimental explanations, and add acknowledgements and explicit appendix cross-references. New limitations and human-study sections shift appendix lettering, but most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds main Table 3 and appendix Table 5 while retaining the existing figures and tables. The larger page canvas introduces wider margins and reflow, including changed algorithm placement; Figure 3's caption updates notation. There is no substantial redesign of the retained visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses two important validation gaps in v1: absent human agreement evidence and untested dependence on the geometry estimator. Appendix E and Table 3 substantially strengthen the metric's empirical justification, while Appendix A clarifies unresolved calibration and tracking limitations. Human correlations cover only 11 aggregate entities without uncertainty for comparative superiority, and estimator tests exclude nuScenes; these constrain the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
